Subject: Exhibit S (Security Controls) — BYO Key handoff playbook & signature options

Hi Emma / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, attached is a targeted redline of the security controls annex we call "Exhibit S" plus an initial draft of a short Key Handoff Playbook that describes the operational steps for importing customer-managed keys (BYOK) into our serving environment. Key points we want to confirm before final execution: 

- BYOK model: customer-managed KMS (imported keys or external KMS integration) with optional emergency escrow. Please confirm whether Greenleaf prefers HSM-backed import or Cloud-KMS integration.
- Rotation window: our standard is a 90-day rotation baseline; for datasets containing sensitive PII we recommend a 30-day rotation. We propose a configurable rotation clause rather than a single fixed value.
- Subprocessor notice: we propose a 30-day advance notice for new subprocessors in Exhibit S rather than 60 days (we can provide immediate notice for high-risk subprocessors).
- Evidence pack: we'll provide SOC 2 Type II PDF, key operation audit logs (redacted), and a dataflow diagram in the shared drive link below.

Attachments: [Attachment: Exhibit_S_redline_v2.pdf] (redlines in tracked changes), [Attachment: Key_Handoff_Playbook_draft.docx] (operational checklist).

Next steps: please review the redline and playbook and tell us whether: (a) you want HSM import vs external-kms integration, (b) you accept configurable rotation with a default of 90 days and option for 30 days on request, and (c) whether your security team needs us to add any additional logging fields in the playbook. Once aligned we can route the final Exhibit S for signature — we support DocuSign and AdobeSign.

For convenience, shared evidence folder: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/security-evidence/greenleaf
DocuSign signing link (optional): https://na1.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&acct=12345&formId=abcd-ef01

Best,

Laura Bennett

Hi Laura — thanks for sending these over. Quick questions from our side after a quick pass: 

1) Can you confirm whether the "emergency escrow" you mention requires a master escrow key held by Redwood, or whether it is a split-escrow model with a third-party custodian? Greenleaf's legal team is sensitive to any possibility of vendor-held master decryption keys.
2) For HSM-backed import: which HSM models and attestation mechanisms do you support? We need FIPS 140-2 Level 3 attestation for our regulated workloads.
3) Rotation: we prefer 30-day rotation for keys used with regulated datasets. If Redwood's default is 90 days, please add a clause to allow per-account rotation policy to be declared in the DPA exhibit.

Can you also drop a current SOC2 report and a minimal data flow diagram so our InfoSec can run a short review? We included a few annotated comments in the attached redline — see "Exhibit_S_greenleaf_redline.pdf" for inline notes.

We intend to route this to procurement/legal this week. Will AdobeSign work for our procurement flow?

Thanks — Emma
Emma Jones
Head of IT Security
Greenleaf Analytics

Emma — thanks for the quick review and the annotated redline. Quoting your key points below for clarity:

On Wed, 12 Aug 2026 at 10:03, emma.jones@greenleaf.ai wrote:
> 1) Can you confirm whether the "emergency escrow" you mention requires a master escrow key held by Redwood, or whether it is a split-escrow model with a third-party custodian?
> 2) For HSM-backed import: which HSM models and attestation mechanisms do you support? We need FIPS 140-2 Level 3 attestation for our regulated workloads.
> 3) Rotation: we prefer 30-day rotation for keys used with regulated datasets. If Redwood's default is 90 days, please add a clause to allow per-account rotation policy to be declared in the DPA exhibit.

Short answers and proposed edits: 
- Emergency escrow: Redwood does NOT hold a vendor-master decryption key. Our standard offering is customer-managed keys with two operational options: (A) direct KMS integration where keys never leave customer's KMS, or (B) an HSM-backed import flow where we hold wrapped keys under an HSM attestation model. For (B) we support split-escrow via a certified third-party custodian (we can add a named custodian in Exhibit S or keep the clause generic). We'll update the redline to explicitly disallow Redwood-held master keys.
- HSM support & attestation: We support AWS CloudHSM import, Azure Dedicated HSM, and common FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSM vendors (Thales, Utimaco). We will add attestation language and the requirement that customers provide a certificate of attestation at import time.
- Rotation policy: Agree to a per-account configurable rotation policy. We'll add language that allows Greenleaf to set a 30-day rotation for regulated datasets while keeping 90 days as a platform default for non-sensitive workloads.

Evidence: attaching a current SOC2 excerpt and adding the dataflow diagram to the shared drive now. Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/security-evidence/greenleaf
Attachments provided: [Attachment: Greenleaf_SOC2_Report.pdf] (redacted), [Drive: dataflow-diagram-greenleaf.png].

Signing: both DocuSign and AdobeSign are supported. Procurement preference: if AdobeSign is required we can generate an AdobeFlow link; otherwise the DocuSign powerform will work. I'll also propose a short 30-minute test window where we can do a key import into a sandbox environment (no production data) so both security teams can validate the playbook.

Proposed meeting times: Thu 13 Aug 11:00am ET or Fri 14 Aug 9:30am ET — let me know what suits.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Director, Enterprise Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
